limits: The default pass asks whether a host that a plugin moved, relocated or removed stranded what rested on or was mounted against it, so it reads a weapon rack held by its neighbours as supported even when another mod disables the room around it. That case is the --empty-space mode (LEFT IN EMPTY SPACE), which refuses exteriors because the land under a fixture is not read.

The --terrain mode reads the terrain as a support, but the engine's triangulation of a heightmap quad is not in the file: where the two possible diagonals disagree the row is cannot tell. evidence.anchor: // PLACEMENT CONTACT — the geometry half of stranded support and orphaned attachment

inputs: Selected plugins/cells, placed geometry and contact criteria.
outputs: Support/contact findings and requested strict overlap evidence; incomplete geometry remains named.

modifiers.--threads: N: the host loop's measuring threads (default 8; 1 is the sequential loop). Results do not depend on it. An explicit N is kept as asked by the memory route, which then only warns.
modifiers.--memory-route: auto|fast|lean|ask (default auto), default pass: decided before the host loop from live data, physical and free memory and any limit (GC heap hard limit, job object). auto: fast when the memory is there; lean when a limit or the machine is too small; when other programs hold the memory, a warning naming them, then lean as the unattended default. fast is the user's answer after closing them; lean the user's refusal; ask stops at that warning with exit 5 and one sentence. A session running contactprobe for a user passes ask, asks the user, and reruns with fast or lean; ordersweep and the evaluation controller never pass it. Nothing fits: exit 2, one sentence. The route, case, readings and warning are in the console and in <emit>.memory.json, which ordersweep copies into summary.json; emit and rows do not depend on the route.
modifiers.--surface: With --overlap-json, write each pair's measured surface contact (crossing length, coplanar areas, area buried in a closed solid), render and collision separately; refusals keep their reason. A pair row may carry aPose/bPose {"dz": d}: that member is measured translated by d in z (a rest pose) and the record echoes it; --volume reads it too, the --json pair review excludes such a row and --anchor refuses it. A pair whose single-precision world placement collapses a triangle is measured in B's frame and labelled pairFrame; particle systems are set aside from a render surface and named (particlesA / particlesB).
modifiers.--live-pose: With --surface, choose the live-pose rule: targeted (default; refuses only what the file shows moving a shape) or blanket (the earlier rule: any controller on the chain refuses).
modifiers.--alpha-visibility: With --surface, a render pair whose crossing lies on an alpha-tested or alpha-blended triangle gains a visibility block: the part of the crossing curve that passes through drawn texels of both members (texture alpha at mip 0, bilinear; alpha test as the interval > .. >= its threshold; blend-only shapes at 0.5 with readings at 0.1 and 0.9 and a threshold-sensitive flag; effect shaders an upper bound), with each texture's VFS source and the base record's alternate texture set applied. A swept witness whose crossing is not opaque x opaque gains visibleMotion (a visible witness at a sampled pose, or no visible crossing at N sampled poses, which is not a never). A missing or unreadable texture or an animated alpha or texture transform refuses the reading by name. Default off: outputs unchanged.
modifiers.--anchor: With --overlap-json, member A of each pair is an anchor (editor marker, idle marker, placed actor, or each furniture entry position) and B a partner: the point, the vertical line and the humanoid body (route constants) at the anchor against B's opaque render surface, the body deciding; Lean furniture excludes its declared support side. With --motion swept, a partner refused for its live pose is tested over every sample of its swept region: witness (a sampled pose meets the body), never (every sample clear by more than its displacement bound), cannot_tell otherwise. Default off: outputs unchanged.
modifiers.--motion: With --surface or --volume, measure a member whose stored pose is not its live pose against its motion instead of refusing it: swept (witness / never / cannot_tell over every animation the files can play, labelled with the animation, cycle, base record type and trigger) or pose:NAME (closed, open, rest - the placed reference's open-by-default flag decides it - state:NAME, <animation>@start|@end). With swept, a pair whose members both move is measured on independent clocks: never; witness only for a held pose (rest, a CLAMP end, a held graph state) against any time of the other with no XESP / XLKR / XAPR link between them in the files; cannot_tell otherwise, naming both times or the link; no volume. A member refused only for a NiPathInterpolator is measured as a tube around its spline (both tangent readings, grown by the subtree radius): never or cannot_tell, never a witness. Swept also applies to --anchor and --box-contact. Default off: outputs unchanged.
modifiers.--motion-delta: With --motion swept, the target bound (u) on how far the moving part moves between samples (default 0.5).
modifiers.--motion-budget: With --motion swept, the samples per animation before the region is reported not converged (default 4096).
modifiers.--force-enable: --force-enable FORMKEY[,FORMKEY...] reads each listed initially-disabled singleton (no enable parent, not itself an enable parent) as enabled after load in every arm, labelled 'enabled by hand (its enabler is not sourced by the switch census)'; a switch member, an enable-parented or already-enabled reference is refused by name (exit 2). The output names every forced reference (forcedEnabled). Default off: outputs unchanged.
modifiers.--cache-budget: --cache-budget SIZE|auto: the byte budget the per-placement contact caches share, and in the default pass the decoded meshes too (least recently used out first; an evicted mesh is decoded again from the same bytes; e.g. 2G, 512M). auto (default) = the smaller of 20 % of the memory the runtime may use and 1 GiB, on either memory route (see --memory-route). Output does not depend on the budget (an evicted grid is rebuilt from the same inputs); a smaller budget can cost time. An explicit size is kept as asked and the memory route only warns.
modifiers.--empty-space: --empty-space FILE selects the empty-space mode: every dependent-scale fixture within reach of a moved host, against that host's mover. LEFT IN EMPTY SPACE when its assembly (what it touches within 4 u, transitively, and the items its weapon racks mount) reached a floor or wall the mover removed or moved, and reaches none under the winner. Interiors only. Rows go to FILE; --emit writes the class as EMPTY-SPACE rows; --base re-measures an emit's rows. A mode of its own: the default pass's outputs are unchanged.
modifiers.--box-contact: With --overlap-json, for each input boxContact row {pairKey, a, b, boxOwner A|B, boxes [{label, min, max}]}, whether each supplied world box (for example a particle region from an overlapprobe manifest's reach parts) meets the other member's placed render surface: opaque triangles, and any material (exact triangle-box test). With --motion swept, a member refused for its live pose is tested through its swept region: witness / never / cannot_tell per box (opaqueMeets true / false / null). Default off: no other output changes.
modifiers.--population: The plan's population file. Default pass: a moved host is judged only when it or a dependent within reach is in the population or its region (the 3x3 cell ring around every position a delta reference takes), so a support another mod placed or removed stays in. With --empty-space: only fixtures of the population's interior cells (closed over references relocated between interiors and rack links) are reported; a fixture ever placed in an exterior is judged too and not reported, so every reported row is the whole-order run's; --base is refused. The emit's population names the file's hash.
modifiers.--population-audit: With --population, EMIT OUT: for each row of another emit (a whole-order run's), whether it is in this population (and, with --empty-space, by which rule).
modifiers.--reverse-of: BASELINE_EMIT, with --base and --emit, default pass only: a reverse run that carries the baseline emit's rows and coverage instead of judging every moved host again, and re-measures only the --base rows; refused by name unless the baseline emit is this run's own (probe, configuration, population, state, measurement policy, instance, and the coverage lines fixed before the host loop). The emit equals a full reverse's.
modifiers.--phase-timers: FILE: the contact code's own time split, for measuring where the time goes: BestContact, PairContact and Judge by sub-phase (dependent soup, broad phase, the caller's placement and base lookups, host grid, the core contact, the radius shells, extent, the authored-depth callback, coverage), each per-placement cache's hits, misses and rebuilds after eviction, the core contact's steps, and how many Measure calls repeat a pair already measured; printed after the run, recorded as run features and written to FILE as JSON. Changes no output.
modifiers.--terrain: Selects the terrain-support mode: every exterior placed reference that rested on the ground (within 4 u) in its placement owner's view, against the winning LAND under both heightmap diagonals and the winning arm's collision supports (render never supports). A row floats or is buried where a plugin the owner could not see reshaped the ground; Introduced Blind Fixed rows of mod plugins are the class and the only emitted rows (TERRAIN); Seen, Inherited (Bethesda on Bethesda), USSEP, Movable and cannot-tell rows are counted. Prints the LAND plumbing and the Inherited floor at 8 / 32 / 128 u before any class count; with --absolute, the absolute floor as shipped first. --emit, --base and --json as in the other modes; the emit declares its population. Requires --float-threshold and --burial-threshold.
modifiers.--float-threshold: With --terrain, the least gap (u) under a body, over the ground and every reference support, that reads Floating. No default: the value is frozen in a run plan.
modifiers.--burial-threshold: With --terrain, the least depth (u) by which the winning ground covers a body's surface that was at or above the authored ground (a part already below it counts nothing), that can read Buried. No default: the value is frozen in a run plan.
modifiers.--burial-share: With --terrain, the least share (0 to 1) of the body's surface in view as authored that the winning ground must cover by more than --burial-threshold for Buried, read on an area-weighted sampling of the body. No default: the value is frozen in a run plan.
modifiers.--terrain-sample: With --terrain --absolute, read the absolute floor on one reference in N (deterministic by FormKey hash, stated on its line); the differential pass is always whole.
